title: Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) — Linear Double Bonds
description: Explore carbon's tetravalency forming two double bonds with oxygens to complete octets.

steps.prompt: In CO₂, carbon forms double bonds with two oxygens. Without lone pairs on the central carbon, what bond angle minimizes repulsion?
steps.explanation: Spot on! The two double bonds repel each other to opposite sides of the carbon nucleus, forming a linear 180° geometry.

steps.prompt: Grab an oxygen atom with your fist and stretch the C=O double bond. Compare the rest length (1.16 Å) with single bonds.
steps.explanation: Double bonds are shorter and stiffer than single bonds because sharing 4 electrons generates a stronger electrostatic pull between the nuclei.

steps.prompt: How many total shared electron pairs exist in one CO₂ molecule?
steps.explanation: Each double bond contains 2 shared pairs, totaling 4 pairs (8 electrons) shared across the molecule.
